title: Multimodal investigation of dacomitinib-calf thymus DNA binding interaction: insights from spectroscopy, thermodynamics, and in-silico studies.
authors: Alossaimi, Manal A; Aldakhil, Taibah; Elmansi, Heba; Belal, Fathalla; Magdy, Galal
one_liner_zh: 该文通过光谱、热力学及分子对接/MD模拟研究小分子药物达克替尼与ctDNA的小沟结合，虽非TF-DNA体系，但属蛋白-DNA互作可迁移的分子结合建模研究，方法上含对接与MD模拟，故给6分。
abstract: Dacomitinib is a second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) used as a first-line targeted therapy for patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. In this study, its interaction with calf thymus DNA (ctDNA) was systematically investigated using UV-Vis spectrophotometry, spectrofluorimetry, viscosity measurements, ionic strength variation, thermodynamic analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The results revealed a strong binding affinity between dacomitinib and ctDNA, with a preferential minor groove-binding mode confirmed through competitive displacement assays using ethidium bromide and rhodamine B, and further supported by UV-Vis and viscosity data. The binding constant (K (b)) at 298 K, calculated using the Benesi-Hildebrand equation, was 7.7 x 10(5) M(-1), indicating high affinity. Thermodynamic parameters (DeltaH degrees  and DeltaS degrees ) indicated that the interaction is primarily governed by van der Waals forces and hydrogen bonding. Frontier molecular orbital (HOMO/LUMO) analysis of dacomitinib showed a wide energy gap, reflecting a favorable tendency for biomolecular interaction. Molecular electrostatic potential (MEP) mapping identified electrophilic and nucleophilic regions and predicted preferential non-covalent interaction sites. Non-Covalent Interaction (NCI) analysis revealed a compact network of van der Waals contacts with minor steric repulsion, supporting conformational stability. Molecular docking confirmed strong, directional, non-covalent affinity toward the DNA minor groove. MD simulations over 100 ns demonstrated structural stability of the dacomitinib-ctDNA complex through stable RMSD, reduced RMSF, compact radius of gyration, and persistent hydrogen bonding. This study provides an integrated experimental and computational analysis of the interaction between dacomitinib and ctDNA, elucidating a non-intercalative minor groove binding mode and offering mechanistic insight into how a targeted kinase inhibitor can engage DNA through shape complementarity, hydrogen bonding, and van der Waals interactions. The observed interaction reflects a binding interaction under in vitro conditions and is not intended to imply a direct role in the established anticancer mechanism of dacomitinib. Beyond characterizing a specific drug-DNA system, these findings highlight general principles governing minor groove recognition by non-classical DNA-binding small molecules and underscore the importance of evaluating potential off-target nucleic acid interactions of targeted therapeutics.
abstract_zh: 达克替尼（Dacomitinib）是一种第二代酪氨酸激酶抑制剂（TKI），用作转移性非小细胞肺癌患者的一线靶向治疗。本研究利用紫外-可见分光光度法、荧光分光光度法、粘度测量、离子强度变化、热力学分析、分子对接和分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟，系统研究了其与小牛胸腺DNA（ctDNA）的相互作用。结果表明，达克替尼与ctDNA之间具有强结合亲和力，并通过溴化乙锭和罗丹明B的竞争性置换实验确认了优先的小沟结合模式，紫外-可见光谱和粘度数据进一步支持了这一结论。利用Benesi-Hildebrand方程计算得到的298 K下结合常数（K(b)）为7.7 x 10(5) M(-1)，表明高亲和力。热力学参数（DeltaH度 和 DeltaS度）表明，该相互作用主要由范德华力和氢键驱动。达克替尼的前线分子轨道（HOMO/LUMO）分析显示其具有较宽的能隙，反映出有利于生物分子相互作用的趋势。分子静电势（MEP）图谱识别了亲电和亲核区域，并预测了优先的非共价相互作用位点。非共价相互作用（NCI）分析揭示了紧凑的范德华接触网络，伴有轻微的空间排斥，支持构象稳定性。分子对接确认了与DNA小沟的强、定向、非共价亲和力。100 ns的MD模拟通过稳定的RMSD、降低的RMSF、紧凑的回转半径和持续的氢键，证明了达克替尼-ctDNA复合物的结构稳定性。本研究提供了达克替尼与ctDNA相互作用的综合实验和计算分析，阐明了一种非嵌入型小沟结合模式，并提供了关于靶向激酶抑制剂如何通过形状互补、氢键和范德华相互作用与DNA结合的机制性见解。观察到的相互作用反映了体外条件下的结合行为，并不旨在暗示其在达克替尼已确立的抗癌机制中具有直接作用。除了表征特定药物-DNA系统外，这些发现还强调了非经典DNA结合小分子识别小沟的一般原理，并突出了评估靶向治疗药物潜在脱靶核酸相互作用的重要性。
